topic: From Intuition to Logic: Mastering Bayes' Theorem & Independence
target_audience: University students in introductory statistics or data science

sections.title: The Foundation: Understanding Independence
lecture_lines: Independence means one event never affects another.
Robot battery levels are separate and independent events.
Multiply individual chances to find the joint probability.
animations: Create two circles, 'City A' (#3498DB) and 'City B' (#E67E22), at opposite sides of the screen.
Place robot 'Bolt' in City A and 'Nut' in City B, both with '50%' labels.
Display the equation P(A ∩ B) = 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25 at the top center in white (#ECF0F1).

sections.title: The Shift: Conditional Probability (Dependency)
lecture_lines: Real-world events often provide clues about each other.
Evidence like footprints shrinks our possible sample space.
Conditional probability measures outcomes given specific information.
animations: Draw a large white rectangle (#ECF0F1) for the Sample Space, with a purple circle (#9B59B6) labeled 'Suspect: Bear'.
Draw a yellow circle (#F1C40F) labeled 'Footprint Found' that partially overlaps the Bear circle.
Fade out the area outside the 'Footprint Found' circle to show the reduced sample space.

sections.title: The Core: Visualizing Bayes' Theorem
lecture_lines: Bayes' Theorem updates our beliefs with new evidence.
Start with the prior: the initial chance of success.
Add the likelihood: how well evidence supports the claim.
Divide by total probability to normalize the result.
This formula calculates the final, updated posterior probability.
animations: Draw a large forest square (#2ECC71) and label it 'Sample Space: 100 Tiles'.
Color a thin vertical strip (1%) gold (#F1C40F) to represent 'Hidden Treasure' (Prior).
In the gold strip, highlight 90% of the area in red (#E74C3C) to show 'True Positive' sensor beeps.
In the remaining green area, highlight a small 10% portion in red (#E74C3C) to show 'False Alarms'.
Display the Bayes' formula P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B) next to the highlighted areas in white (#ECF0F1).

sections.title: Step-by-Step Application: The Medical Test Paradox
lecture_lines: Rare events make high-accuracy tests very counter-intuitive.
Most positive results come from the healthy population.
Tree diagrams help map true versus false positives.
Bayesian logic explains why rare diseases have low certainty.
Always consider base rates before interpreting individual results.
animations: Draw a tree diagram starting from '1000 Penguins' at the top center (#ECF0F1).
Create two branches: '1 Sick' (#3498DB) and '999 Healthy' (#27AE60).
From '1 Sick', draw a branch to '1 Positive Test' (#E74C3C); from '999 Healthy', branch to '10 Positive Tests' (#E74C3C).
Circle all 'Positive Test' outcomes (1 true positive, 10 false positives) in yellow (#F1C40F) to show the new sample space.
Write the calculation 1 / (1 + 10) ≈ 9% to show the final probability in white (#ECF0F1).

sections.title: Summary: The Bayesian Mindset
lecture_lines: Bayes' Theorem is a tool for updating our worldview.
Turn initial hypotheses into evidence-based conclusions.
Master the logic of uncertainty for better data science.
animations: Draw a horizontal sliding scale with 'Initial Guess' on the left and 'Truth' on the right (#ECF0F1).
Animate a yellow 'Evidence' icon (#F1C40F) falling onto the scale.
Move the scale's pointer (#E67E22) from the far left towards the right based on the evidence.
